estrutura.personaBrief: Basis: law in force. Colombia is a unitary state (Constitution art. 1) with a single national police, governors acting as agents of the president (arts. 303/305) and constitutional fiscal transfers. The 'pais de regiones' talk has no bill, so it only breaks ties; no formal act changes the unitary framework.

representacao.personaBrief: Basis: formal acts and law in force. Effective democracy: alternation of power happened, the opposition leads the Senate under the Opposition Statute, courts and the Central Bank act independently and the executive complied with judges. Decree 1446 and Directive 01 are criticised but do not break institutional pluralism; reelection is constitutionally banned.

poder.personaBrief: Basis: formal acts for security (ended talks, bombings, mega-prisons, extraditions, lifting of the carry-permit suspension) and law in force elsewhere (death penalty banned by art. 11, personal drug dose decriminalised, euthanasia legal by Constitutional Court ruling, habeas corpus). Securitarian on policing and surveillance, bound by constitutional limits on the rest.

imigracao.personaBrief: Basis: mix of formal act and law in force. The order of 23-Aug-2026 to identify and deport irregular migrants (offenders first) pushes toward restriction, while the Temporary Protection Statute for 2.8 million Venezuelans stays in force and the Constitution recognises a multiethnic nation with ethnic-group languages.

diplomacia.personaBrief: Basis: formal acts. Resolutions ended the 'paz total' dialogues, bombings resumed, the Americas Shield pact with the US was joined and mandatory military service (Law 1861) continues; the 2027 Defence budget came in below the military's request, and nuclear weapons or a first strike war are outside the legal and political frame.

intervencao.personaBrief: Basis: formal acts and alignment announcements. Joining the Americas Shield with authorised joint operations, extraditions to the US, non-recognition of Delcy Rodriguez and cutting ties with Cuba and Nicaragua show an assertive, US-aligned foreign policy; treaties still bind through the Constitution's block of constitutionality.

economia.personaBrief: Basis: formal acts plus law in force. Spending freeze, merging ministries and liquidating the Equality Ministry point to a smaller state, but Ecopetrol and other state firms remain public with no sale announced, and targeted subsidies and public banks continue; the mixed private-public health and public service system stays.

controle.personaBrief: Basis: law in force and some acts. The Central Bank's constitutional autonomy was respected (rate raised to 12.25% against the government's preference), the minimum wage is set by law and a progressive tax principle holds; the government pushes spending freeze, tax cuts and deregulation, though it reportedly reversed a fuel price rise (a tie-break, not a formal act).

comercio.personaBrief: Basis: announcements with no protectionist act. The inauguration speech promised to widen free trade agreements and cut tariffs, the government negotiates the removal of the US 12.5% tariff and has not raised tariffs of its own; Colombian law keeps some national preference in procurement.

religiao.personaBrief: Basis: formal court rulings and the Constitution (secular state, freedom of worship, God invoked in the preamble) versus the president's personal Catholic practice. Judges forced an apology and a halt to official confessional acts and he complied, so the State remains secular in law while its leader and cabinet appointments favour religion.

moral.personaBrief: Basis: law in force with tie-breaks from the government's orientation. Court rulings on abortion up to week 24, equal marriage, adoption and gender ID remain in force with no formal act against them, but the government's moral profile (pro-life and pro-family commitment, Education Minister from the 2017 referendum campaign) is conservative.

tecnologia.personaBrief: Basis: announcements with no decree yet, plus law in force. Pro-growth agenda: 'responsible' fracking outside paramos and Amazon, large-scale agribusiness in the Orinoquia and AI in tax collection; mining in protected areas stays legally restricted.
